newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel inflation-linked bonds up ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israel inflation-linked bonds up ahead of CPI.

text.p: Israeli long bonds linked to inflation rose on Thursday ahead of the release on Friday of October's consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years):
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 160.14
Volume was low at 150 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds, which closed flat after two straight weeks of gains, traders said.

"Trading was mixed today with inflation-linked long bonds posting the highest rise. Yields (in the long bonds) have fallen from 5.25 percent in August to 4.45 percent. The short series were stable, closing almost unchanged," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House.

"Activity in the long bonds was affected by hopes for a low October CPI. The official forecasts are for a rise of 0.9 percent, but investors hope for a lower figure," said Baruch Glicksberg at Clal Insurance.
Traders believe that if the CPI comes in at 0.7-0.9 percent the Bank of Israel will reduce short-term rates by 0.5 percentage point.
Traders said unlinked bonds were stable after two weeks of sharp rises.
"Most of the activity was concentrated in the unlinked bonds which closed almost unchanged. At the current rate the market has reached an equilibrium," Weisberg said.
"The Makams continue to rise with yields (in one-year Makams) falling in two weeks from 15.5 percent to 15.2 percent. Volume was very low today at 28 million shekels," Glicksberg added.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds continued to fall in response to the dollar's recent weakness against the shekel.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
